newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee holds against dollar on SBI purchases.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee holds against dollar on SBI purchases.

text.p: The State Bank of India (SBI) bought dollars on Monday, helping the Indian rupee hold against the U.S. currency, dealers said.
The rupee was trading steady at 35.71/72 at early noon.
The rupee was expected to rise against the dollar on Monday and dealers were looking to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to intervene by purchasing dollars, as it had done on Friday.
On Friday RBI bought dollars when the rupee broke through the 35.70-mark to trade briefly at 35.69 against dollar.
"There is some corporate demand today," said a dealer.
"But the volumes are very thin because lot of (bank and company) staff could not attend offices," he said.
A section of the Central Railway suburban rail system was disrupted on Monday because of a strike in parts of Maharashtra state.
